key_insight: Shallow QAOA mixer design faces two complementary bottlenecks: probability transport through configuration space and finite-depth causal reach across the problem graph.
engineering_relevance: Problem-aligned two-qubit mixer interactions can improve approximation ratios at equal QAOA depth, but greater causal reach alone does not guarantee better performance.
method: Derive first-order objective bounds in small-β and small-γ regimes, linked by a graph-Laplacian identity for connected regular mixer graphs.
Bound attainable objectives non-perturbatively using layer-wise ℓ₁ spreading of the mixer unitary.
Evaluate X+XX and X+YY mixers for MaxCut; the k-hop construction has causal radius at most (k+1)p.
evidence_signal: Across cycles, circular ladders, and high-girth regular bipartite graphs, both augmented mixers improved best-found equal-depth ratios; in examined reach-matched cases, X+YY at depth p came within about one approximation-ratio point of X at depth 2p.
watch_item: The numerical gains are best-found results on selected graph families, and equal causal reach does not imply equal performance.
paper_title: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach
